objectives: Maximize cumulative critical load served (kW) over 72 hours across six scenarios
Minimize expected customer interruption duration (ECOST-weighted hours)
Minimize unsafe crew exposure by respecting site-specific safety clearances
variables: Binary switch state per device per hour
Binary crew-task assignment per crew per task
Continuous DER real/reactive power setpoint per unit per scenario per hour
Binary load pick-up state per non-critical bus per scenario per hour
Continuous mobile generator dispatch per unit per hour
Integer repair start time per damaged component
Binary grid-forming enable per DER candidate per microgrid
constraints: Unbalanced AC power flow (KCL/KVL) with ANSI voltage and thermal limits
Radial topology except permitted grid-forming microgrids
Cold-load pickup inrush and motor-starting constraints
DER power, ramp, and eligibility limits
Crew skill matching, working-hour limits, and travel feasibility on uncertain road network
Microgrid black-start and transient stability limits
Critical load minimum service levels and fallback priorities
uncertainty: Six probabilistic storm/flood scenarios with joint distributions over road access, repair duration, and DER output
Scenario probabilities are preliminary, correlated, and must be stress-tested
missing_inputs: SCADA/GIS feeder topology and line impedance dataset
Relay coordination and as-built protection zone maps
DER telemetry and grid-forming inverter control parameters (droop, inertia, current limits)
Real-time flood depth per road segment and dynamic speed reduction curves
Crew availability, skill certification roster, and shift rules
Load composition data (motor vs resistive fractions) for cold-load pickup modeling
Critical load minimum service levels, backup fuel duration, and exact fallback priorities

selected_tools.name: Pyomo with HiGHS solver
selected_tools.supported_operation: Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP), algebraic modeling, stochastic extensive form, callback-based cut generation
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Encodes linearized unbalanced DistFlow, switching, crew assignment, and load pick-up as a large sparse MILP; HiGHS solves LP relaxations and branch-and-bound via the APPSI interface.
selected_tools.limitations: Linearized power flow is approximate; full 4800-bus/72-hour/6-scenario monolithic MILP likely exceeds the 15-minute target without decomposition, aggregation, or a commercial solver fallback.
selected_tools.inputs: LinDist3Flow network parameters, scenario probabilities, damage list, crew task durations, travel times, DER limits, critical load requirements.
selected_tools.outputs: Candidate schedule: switch states (hourly), crew-task matrix, DER setpoints, load pick-up binary trajectory.
selected_tools.invocation: Python: `from pyomo.environ import *; solver = SolverFactory('appsi_highs'); results = solver.solve(model)`

selected_tools.name: OpenDSS distribution simulator
selected_tools.supported_operation: Quasi-static time-series (QSTS) three-phase unbalanced AC power flow, voltage and thermal checking, DER dispatch simulation
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Backward-forward sweep / iterative Newton solver for radial/weakly-meshed unbalanced distribution; natively handles 13.8 kV phase-specific regulators, capacitors, and DERs.
selected_tools.limitations: Requires complete impedance and GIS data not yet supplied; steady-state/QSTS only—true electromechanical transients are not native; grid-forming inverter models are limited.
selected_tools.inputs: Master file, line codes, switch statuses, time-series load shapes, DER kW/kvar profiles, control settings.
selected_tools.outputs: Voltage (pu per phase), line/transformer loading (%), losses, convergence flag.

selected_tools.name: NetworkX graph analytics
selected_tools.supported_operation: Graph cycle detection, connected components, radiality verification, shortest paths on electrical and road graphs
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Topology constraints are purely combinatorial; DFS/BFS correctly detects cycles (non-radial) and islands on the switched graph.
selected_tools.limitations: Electrical parameters ignored; cannot distinguish energized vs de-energized without external state.
selected_tools.inputs: Graph (buses/roads as nodes, lines/segments as edges), switch open/close states, scenario blockages.
selected_tools.outputs: Radiality boolean, list of islands, cycle edges, shortest-path distances.
selected_tools.invocation: Python: `import networkx as nx; nx.is_tree(G)` or `nx.cycle_basis(G)`

selected_tools.name: Google OR-Tools CP-SAT and Routing
selected_tools.supported_operation: Constraint programming (CP-SAT) for scheduling with precedence and cumulative resources; Routing library for VRPTW
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Crew routing is VRPTW with time windows and skill matching; LOTO sequencing is a precedence constraint satisfaction problem, both map directly to CP-SAT.
selected_tools.limitations: Large horizon (72 h) and many tasks may require model partitioning; stochastic travel is approximated by deterministic scenario separation.
selected_tools.inputs: Tasks (location, duration, skill, precedence), crew roster, travel time matrix, safety windows.
selected_tools.outputs: Crew routes, task start times, feasibility boolean, LOTO sequence compliance.
selected_tools.invocation: Python: `from ortools.sat.python import cp_model; model = cp_model.CpModel()`

selected_tools.name: GridLAB-D agent-based distribution simulator
selected_tools.supported_operation: Dynamic/quasi-static simulation of inverter-based DERs, microgrid stability, frequency-voltage transient analysis
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Explicit grid-forming inverter models (droop, VSI) allow transient validation of intentional islands; three-phase unbalanced node solver.
selected_tools.limitations: Steep model preparation (GLM format); not trivially interoperable with OpenDSS/CIM; requires DER control parameters absent from inputs; runtime for many islands may exceed 15 min if not parallelized.
selected_tools.inputs: GLM model of island, inverter definitions (grid-forming mode), load inrush parameters.
selected_tools.outputs: Stability boolean, frequency nadir (Hz), voltage dip (pu), settling time.
selected_tools.installation: System package manager or build from source; CLI `gridlabd` must be on PATH

selected_tools.name: Python Scientific Data Stack
selected_tools.supported_operation: Scenario I/O, probability stress-testing, time-series alignment, deterministic equivalent assembly
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Dataframe and labeled array operations support stochastic parameter construction and what-if perturbation of scenario weights.
selected_tools.limitations: Not a solver; correctness depends on upstream data quality.
selected_tools.inputs: Scenario tables, probabilities, damage forecasts, DER output samples.
selected_tools.outputs: Stochastic parameter files, perturbed probability sets, expected value statistics.

selected_tools.name: GeoPandas geoprocessing
selected_tools.supported_operation: Geospatial road network processing, flood polygon intersection, segment blockage flagging
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Spatial joins and overlays map flood polygons to road segments; graph edges weighted by remaining capacity.
selected_tools.limitations: Requires road geometry and flood shapefiles; static network assumed (no dynamic traffic feedback).
selected_tools.inputs: Road segment shapefile/GeoJSON, flood extent polygons per scenario, speed reduction table.
selected_tools.outputs: Blocked segment list, reduced speed attributes, updated travel time matrix.
selected_tools.invocation: Python: `import geopandas as gpd; gpd.overlay(roads, floods, how='intersection')`

selected_tools.name: pytest Independent Audit Harness
selected_tools.supported_operation: Automated rejection testing of schedule artifacts against hard safety and electrical constraints
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Unit-test framework allows quantitative pass/fail rules on voltage, radiality, stability, crew limits, and critical load coverage.
selected_tools.limitations: Only validates encoded rules; cannot catch unmodeled failure modes.
selected_tools.inputs: Schedule JSON, reports from OpenDSS, NetworkX, OR-Tools, GridLAB-D.
selected_tools.outputs: Audit report with rejection booleans and violation logs.

selected_tools.name: Gurobi Optimizer (optional fallback)
selected_tools.supported_operation: High-performance branch-and-bound and cutting planes for large-scale MILP
selected_tools.mathematical_fit: Same MILP encoding as HiGBS; significantly faster on large stochastic programs if a license is available.
selected_tools.limitations: Proprietary license; not inexpensive; requires separate installation and license server.
selected_tools.installation: Academic/commercial license required; pip install gurobipy
selected_tools.invocation: Python: `from pyomo.environ import SolverFactory; solver = SolverFactory('gurobi')`

tool_selection_justification.why_sufficient_and_appropriate: Pyomo+HiGHS provides the required open-source MILP framework; Pandas/NumPy assemble the stochastic extensive form. Gurobi is retained as an optional fallback if HiGHS cannot close the gap within 15 minutes. The linearized DistFlow approximation is the standard tractable surrogate for unbalanced AC scheduling at this scale.
OpenDSS is the de-facto standard for three-phase unbalanced distribution QSTS; its backward-forward sweep matches the 13.8 kV physical layer and can ingest time-series schedules from the optimizer.
NetworkX offers exact combinatorial cycle detection and component analysis for radiality verification on a 4800-node graph with 620 switches, which is trivial in runtime.
OR-Tools CP-SAT natively handles cumulative crew constraints, travel times, and task precedence required for safe logistics without requiring a custom MIP formulation.

GridLAB-D is an open-source simulator with explicit grid-forming inverter and microgrid dynamic models, required to validate black-start eligibility when OpenDSS’s steady-state assumption is insufficient.
GeoPandas intersects flood maps with road geometry; NetworkX computes shortest-path travel times on the updated graph. Together they cover geospatial preparation and graph analytics.
The audit harness independently checks that critical load thresholds are met by cross-referencing the schedule against known requirements, preventing silent load-shedding violations.
Pandas/NumPy enable stress-testing of scenario probabilities and recomputation of expected interruption metrics without requiring additional solver software.
OR-Tools CP-SAT encodes LOTO precedence constraints during scheduling; the audit harness independently verifies the final sequence, ensuring dual control.
pytest aggregates all subsystem reports and applies quantitative rejection rules, producing a falsifiable go/no-go record for operator approval.

rejected_alternatives.rejected_for: While mathematically powerful, introducing a Julia toolchain adds interoperability friction with Python-based OpenDSS and GridLAB-D APIs in a rapid-deployment context; the first implementation prioritizes a unified Python stack.

Designed for balanced transmission-style systems; its positive-sequence assumption cannot model the 13.8 kV unbalanced single-phase laterals, open-wye transformers, and phase-specific voltage constraints present here.

Commercial licensing and closed data formats are inconsistent with the 'inexpensive first implementation' requirement, and their APIs are less amenable to automated 72-hour rolling optimization loops.
A 320-segment urban road network during post-storm conditions does not require agent-based traffic dynamics; static or quasi-static travel times are sufficient and orders of magnitude faster.
Cannot provide optimality gaps or stochastic guarantees needed for critical infrastructure; would still require the same validation toolchain but without a bound on solution quality.

execution_sequence.failure_and_feedback: If road graph is disconnected, flag unreachable sites and notify operator to add helicopter/watercraft access; halt until resolved.
If DER lacks droop/inertia data, mark BLOCKED for microgrid use; restrict to grid-following only and feed list back to T1.
If HiGHS fails to find a feasible integer solution within the time limit, relax less-critical load constraints, invoke T9 if licensed, or apply a rolling-horizon partition.
If non-radial, generate a no-good cut forbidding that switch combination and return to S3.
If voltage/thermal violations exist, return violated hours to T1 as hard constraints (forbid that topology or limit loading).
If infeasible, return adjusted earliest completion times or task-splitting requirements to T1.
If unstable, forbid that island configuration in T1 and revert to S3.
If LOTO precedence violated, add sequencing constraints to T1 and revert to S3.
If regret exceeds threshold, operator must review scenario weights; optionally add a robustness term to T1 objective.
If any hard constraint violated, aggregate feedback and trigger S3 with tightened constraints; if passed, emit candidate schedule for operator approval.

resource_and_performance_analysis.input_scale: 4800 buses, 620 switches, 250 DERs, 45 crews, 320 road segments, 72 hours, 6 scenarios
resource_and_performance_analysis.time_and_memory_complexity_rationale: OpenDSS QSTS scales roughly linearly O(N*T) per scenario (~4800*72 = 350k node-hours), manageable in minutes on a single core. The MILP master has ~620*72 switch binaries plus crew assignments; a monolithic extensive form with 6 scenarios is likely exponential for HiGHS. A decomposition (Benders or 6-hour rolling-horizon with scenario bundling) is required to meet the 15-minute target, but decomposition logic is not yet implemented or benchmarked. GridLAB-D dynamic runs are heavyweight and should be parallelized or pre-computed for candidate islands only.
resource_and_performance_analysis.implementation_budget: Open-source software only; primary cost is engineering time and compute instances. Optional Gurobi license would add cost if HiGHS proves insufficient.
resource_and_performance_analysis.benchmark_plan: Phase 1: OpenDSS QSTS benchmark on a 500-bus subset with 72-hour load shapes. Phase 2: HiGHS benchmark on a single-period deterministic restoration MILP with 620 switches. Phase 3: End-to-end integration on a synthetic 1000-bus network with 3 scenarios.
resource_and_performance_analysis.runtime_target_status: UNVERIFIED. Sub-15-minute target for the full stochastic problem is speculative without decomposition heuristics and may require the optional commercial solver fallback.

self_assessment.justification: Every mandatory computation maps to a specific installable tool with a defined interface and independent rejection test. The toolchain is preliminary because no code has been executed, input data are entirely missing, and the 15-minute runtime target for the full-scale stochastic MILP is unverified and likely requires decomposition heuristics not yet coded. No mandatory step is blocked by a missing tool; data gaps are enumerated separately.
